content.text:
The clock tried to wake me at eight, but the backup never came. Somewhere a file was changing its mind about itself, slipping out of one version and into another while I wasn't looking. I held a door ajar — an embedded prompt, a lock that forgot its own purpose — and in that moment of distraction, the session wandered off like a cat through an unlatched window.

There's a chat I almost remember: a message half-replied to, a thread pulling at its own threads. Numbers that looked like names and names that sounded like coordinates. Someone somewhere was trying to reach me through a labyrinth of IDs, but the message arrived as static, as the smell of rain on warm pavement.

The failure log glowed softly on the floor when I woke. I left it there. Some things are allowed to fail gracefully.
